translation:
Treats injury to the liver from pent-up anger, with the eyes red, irritated, and dim. It is common in women, with blood-deficiency fever, dry mouth, spontaneous sweating, irregular menstruation, abdominal pain, and similar syndromes.

Large Danggui (washed with wine, 1 qian), Baishaoyao (stir-fried in wine, 1 qian), Bai Fushen (skin removed, 1 qian), Baizhu (stir-fried in earth, 1 qian), Bei Chaihu (stir-fried, 1 qian), Mudanpi (1 qian), Su Bohe (3 fen), Gancao (3 fen), Chuan Huanglian (3 fen, stir-fried with a decoction of Wuzhuyu).

Cut the above into slices and decoct in water. The ancient formula has Zhizi kernel, but Master Zhao, fearing it would injure the stomach qi, removed it.
translator_notes: 大當歸 (large Danggui) means high-quality Danggui.
蘇薄荷 (Su Bohe) refers to mint from Suzhou.
趙氏 (Master Zhao) cannot be identified with certainty.
